 More rainy weather for today and tomorrow 
 By Justin Loew 
 Justin Loew 
 Author email 
 Nov 3, 2026 
 Nov 3, 2026 
 Updated 
 Nov 3, 2026

 Weather
 More cloudy and damp weather is on the way. It will not dry up until Thursday afternoon, when the weather will be turning cooler as well. 
 Today: Cloudy, breezy, warm, and humid with off-and-on rain and maybe a few rumbles of thunder.
 High: 65 Wind: South 10-20
 Tonight: Overcast and mild with periods of rain.
 Low: 60 Wind: SE 10-15
 Wednesday: Steady rain early, tapering to spotty showers and drizzle in the afternoon. Cloudy again.
 High: 60 early, then falling into the 50s Wind: SE 10-20, becoming SW
 Off-and-on rain, isolated thundershowers, and cloudy skies will be the rule for this Tuesday. It will also be warm and kind-of humid for this time of year. Highs will be in the 60s, and it will be breezy. Winds will be out of the south at 10 to 20 mph. Rain amounts will likely be in the quarter to half-inch range.
 A more steady rain could develop later tonight into early Wednesday morning, then by midday Wednesday the rain will become more spotty and light. It will still be cloudy tomorrow, with temperatures dropping into the 50s.
 The temperature drop will continue into Thursday when highs will only reach the upper 40s. The weather will be damp with light showers and drizzle Thursday morning, then it will dry up during the afternoon, but remain fairly cloudy.
 More sun should develop on Friday and highs will be in the 40s, so it will feel more like the season. Dry weather should then continue for the most part through early next week. There will be a mixture of clouds and sun from Saturday through Tuesday, and high temperatures will be above normal. The mercury should reach the low 50s on Saturday, the low to mid 50s on Sunday, and the mid to upper 50s on Monday.
 Have a spectacular Tuesday, Morning Update, 3 – November 2026, Meteorologist Justin Loew
 On this date in weather history: 1927 — Historic flooding occurred across Vermont from November 2nd through the 4th. The flood washed out 1285 bridges, miles of roads and railways, and several homes and buildings. Eighty-four people were killed from the flooding, including Lt. Governor S. Hollister Jackson.
